subproblem.title: Blow-up (L. Simon) estimate on the unit ball: [Dw]_{alpha;B_1/2} <= delta K + C_delta (S + G)
subproblem.statement: Let n >= 1 and l be natural numbers, 0 < alpha < 1, lam > 0, M real and delta > 0. Let L := L(R^n, R^l) and B_1 := B_1(0). There is a constant C_delta >= 0 with the following property. Let a : R^n -> (continuous bilinear forms on L), Phi : R^n -> (continuous linear forms on L), w : R^n -> R^l and reals K, S, G with G >= 0 satisfy, for all x, y in B_1 and P, Q in L: lam ||P||^2 <= a(x)[P][P]; |a(x)[P][Q]| <= M ||P|| ||Q||; |a(x)[P][Q] - a(y)[P][Q]| <= M |x - y|^alpha ||P|| ||Q||; |Phi(x)[P] - Phi(y)[P]| <= G |x - y|^alpha ||P||; |w(x)| <= S. Assume moreover that w is C^1 on B_1, that ||Dw(x) - Dw(y)|| <= K |x - y|^alpha for x, y in B_1, and that the integral over B_1 of a(x)[Dw(x)][Dzeta(x)] equals the integral over B_1 of Phi(x)[Dzeta(x)] for every C^1 compactly supported zeta : R^n -> R^l with tsupport zeta in B_1. Then ||Dw(x) - Dw(y)|| <= (delta K + C_delta (S + G)) |x - y|^alpha for all x, y in B_{1/2}(0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ α : ℝ, 0 < α → α < 1 → ∀ lam M δ : ℝ, 0 < lam → 0 < δ → ∃ Cδ : ℝ, 0 ≤ Cδ ∧ ∀ (a : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (Φ : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (w : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (K S G : ℝ), 0 ≤ G → (∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) 1, ∀ P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, lam * ‖P‖ ^ 2 ≤ a x P P) → (∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) 1, ∀ P Q : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, |a x P Q| ≤ M * ‖P‖ * ‖Q‖) → (∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) 1, ∀ y ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) 1, ∀ P Q : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, |a x P Q - a y P Q| ≤ M * ‖x - y‖ ^ α * ‖P‖ * ‖Q‖) → (∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) 1, ∀ y ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) 1, ∀ P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, |Φ x P - Φ y P| ≤ G * ‖x - y‖ ^ α * ‖P‖) → (∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) 1, ‖w x‖ ≤ S) → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 w (ball (0 : Rn n) 1) → (∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) 1, ∀ y ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) 1, ‖fderiv ℝ w x - fderiv ℝ w y‖ ≤ K * ‖x - y‖ ^ α) → (∀ ζ : Rn n → Rn ℓ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → tsupport ζ ⊆ ball (0 : Rn n) 1 → ∫ x in ball (0 : Rn n) 1, a x (fderiv ℝ w x) (fderiv ℝ ζ x) = ∫ x in ball (0 : Rn n) 1, Φ x (fderiv ℝ ζ x)) → ∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) (1 / 2), ∀ y ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) (1 / 2), ‖fderiv ℝ w x - fderiv ℝ w y‖ ≤ (δ * K + Cδ * (S + G)) * ‖x - y‖ ^ α
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof. This is the blow-up argument of L. Simon, Schauder estimates by scaling, Calc. Var. PDE 5 (1997) 391-407; the scalar divergence-form case is in S. Vita, arXiv:2510.01765, Sect. 5. Here it is written with arbitrary admissible constants K (for the Hoelder seminorm of Dw on B_1), S (for sup |w|) and G (for the Hoelder seminorm of Phi). This form is equivalent to the parent's seminorm form, since every admissible K, S, G dominates the corresponding seminorm.
Notation. B_1 := B_1(0), B_{1/2} := B_{1/2}(0), L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm. A tuple (a, Phi, w, K, S, G) is admissible if G >= 0 and all hypotheses of the statement hold. Since n >= 1, B_1 contains two distinct points. So for admissible data, K >= 0 (from 0 <= ||Dw(x) - Dw(y)|| <= K |x - y|^alpha with x != y), and S >= |w(0)| >= 0.
0. Preliminaries.
 (0a) Trivial cases. If l = 0, then L = {0}, Dw = 0, and the right side (delta K + C (S + G)) |x - y|^alpha is >= 0 for any C >= 0; so C_delta := 0 works. If l >= 1 and M < lam, no admissible data exist: for P != 0 in L and x = 0, lam ||P||^2 <= a(0)[P][P] <= M ||P||^2 < lam ||P||^2. So again C_delta := 0 works. From now on assume l >= 1 and M >= lam > 0.
 (0b) Continuity of integrands. For admissible data and fixed P, Q in L, x -> a(x)[P][Q] and x -> Phi(x)[P] are continuous on B_1 by the Hoelder hypotheses. Expanding P(x), Q(x) in a basis of L shows that x -> a(x)[P(x)][Q(x)] and x -> Phi(x)[Q(x)] are continuous on every open subset of B_1 where P(.) and Q(.) are continuous. Hence every integrand below of the form a(x)[Dv(x)][Dzeta(x)] or Phi(x)[Dzeta(x)] is continuous with compact support after extension by 0. Here v is C^1 on the relevant open set and zeta is C^1 with compact support inside it. Such integrands are integrable, which justifies the linear manipulations of integrals below.
1. Contradiction hypothesis. Suppose the statement fails for the given delta. Then for every k in N, taking C_delta := k, there are admissible data (a_k, Phi_k, w_k, K_k, S_k, G_k) and points x_k, y_k in B_{1/2} with ||Dw_k(x_k) - Dw_k(y_k)|| > (delta K_k + k (S_k + G_k)) |x_k - y_k|^alpha. Then x_k != y_k, since otherwise both sides are 0 (0^alpha = 0). Put s_k := ||Dw_k(x_k) - Dw_k(y_k)|| / |x_k - y_k|^alpha. Then s_k > delta K_k + k (S_k + G_k) >= 0.
2. Normalization. Replace w_k, Phi_k, K_k, S_k, G_k by w_k/s_k, Phi_k/s_k, K_k/s_k, S_k/s_k, G_k/s_k, and keep a_k. Admissibility persists: D(w_k/s_k) = Dw_k/s_k on B_1, and the weak equation is linear in (w, Phi). Now ||Dw_k(x_k) - Dw_k(y_k)|| = |x_k - y_k|^alpha and delta K_k + k (S_k + G_k) < 1. So for k >= 1: K_k < 1/delta, S_k < 1/k and G_k < 1/k. Thus on B_1: ||Dw_k(x) - Dw_k(y)|| <= delta^{-1} |x - y|^alpha, |w_k| <= 1/k, and |Phi_k(x)[P] - Phi_k(y)[P]| <= k^{-1} |x - y|^alpha ||P||.
3. Small gradients (parent 5b). Let k >= 5 and x in B_{1/2}. Then B_{1/2}(x) is contained in B_1. Apply the sibling interpolation lemma on B_{1/2}(x) with S := 1/k, K := 1/delta and t := k^{-1/2} < 1/2. It gives ||Dw_k(x)|| <= 2 k^{-1/2} + k^{-alpha/2}/delta =: eps_k, and eps_k -> 0.
4. The scale tends to 0 (parent 5c). Let rho_k := |x_k - y_k|, which lies in (0, 1). Then rho_k^alpha = ||Dw_k(x_k) - Dw_k(y_k)|| <= 2 eps_k -> 0, so rho_k -> 0. Passing to a tail of the sequence, assume k >= 5 and rho_k < 1/2 for all k considered.
5. Blow-up (parent 5d). Let D_k := B_{1/(2 rho_k)}(0), P_k := Dw_k(x_k) (so ||P_k|| <= eps_k), and W_k(z) := rho_k^{-1-alpha} [w_k(x_k + rho_k z) - w_k(x_k) - rho_k P_k z]. For z in D_k, x_k + rho_k z lies in B_{1/2}(x_k), which is contained in B_1 because |x_k| < 1/2. Apply the sibling rescale lemma with U := B_1, y := x_k, rho := rho_k, z0 := 0 and r := 1/(2 rho_k). Its ball B_{rho_k r}(x_k) = B_{1/2}(x_k) is contained in B_1. The lemma shows that wt_k(z) := w_k(x_k + rho_k z) is C^1 on D_k with Dwt_k(z) = rho_k Dw_k(x_k + rho_k z). Hence W_k is C^1 on D_k, W_k(0) = 0, DW_k(z) = rho_k^{-alpha} [Dw_k(x_k + rho_k z) - P_k] and DW_k(0) = 0. For z, z' in D_k, ||DW_k(z) - DW_k(z')|| = rho_k^{-alpha} ||Dw_k(x_k + rho_k z) - Dw_k(x_k + rho_k z')|| <= delta^{-1} |z - z'|^alpha. In particular ||DW_k(z)|| <= delta^{-1} |z|^alpha, and by the mean value inequality on the segment [0, z], which lies in D_k, |W_k(z)| <= delta^{-1} |z|^{1+alpha}. Let e_k := (y_k - x_k)/rho_k. Then |e_k| = 1, e_k is in D_k (since 1 < 1/(2 rho_k)), and ||DW_k(e_k)|| = rho_k^{-alpha} ||Dw_k(y_k) - Dw_k(x_k)|| = 1.
6. Rescaled equation (parent 5e). Let A_k := a_k(x_k) and ah_k(z) := a_k(x_k + rho_k z). For z in D_k define the linear form Psi_k(z)[Q] := rho_k^{-alpha} (Phi_k(x_k + rho_k z)[Q] - Phi_k(x_k)[Q]) - rho_k^{-alpha} (a_k(x_k + rho_k z)[P_k][Q] - A_k[P_k][Q]). Let zeta be C^1 with compact support and tsupport zeta in D_k. Part (iii) of the rescale lemma gives: integral over D_k of ah_k[Dwt_k][Dzeta] = integral over D_k of rho_k Phi_k(x_k + rho_k z)[Dzeta]. The sibling zero_mean lemma, applied to the constant linear forms c = A_k[P_k][.] and c = Phi_k(x_k), gives integral of A_k[P_k][Dzeta] = 0 = integral of Phi_k(x_k)[Dzeta]. These integrals are over R^n and equal the integrals over D_k, because the integrands vanish outside tsupport zeta. On D_k we have Dwt_k = rho_k P_k + rho_k^{1+alpha} DW_k. By bilinearity and (0b):
 rho_k^{1+alpha} (integral over D_k of ah_k[DW_k][Dzeta])
 = (integral over D_k of rho_k Phi_k(x_k + rho_k z)[Dzeta]) - rho_k (integral over D_k of ah_k[P_k][Dzeta])
 = rho_k (integral over D_k of (Phi_k(x_k + rho_k z) - Phi_k(x_k))[Dzeta]) - rho_k (integral over D_k of (ah_k - A_k)[P_k][Dzeta]).
 Dividing by rho_k^{1+alpha} gives: integral over D_k of ah_k[DW_k][Dzeta] = integral over D_k of Psi_k[Dzeta]. Bounds for z in D_k and P, Q in L follow from the Hoelder hypotheses at the points x_k + rho_k z and x_k of B_1, and from M >= 0: |Psi_k(z)[Q]| <= (1/k + M eps_k) |z|^alpha ||Q||, and |ah_k(z)[P][Q] - A_k[P][Q]| <= M rho_k^alpha |z|^alpha ||P|| ||Q||.
7. Compactness (parent 5f). Fix a basis E_1..E_N of L and a constant c_L with sum_r |P_r| <= c_L ||P|| for the coordinates P = sum_r P_r E_r. The real numbers A_k[E_r][E_s] are bounded by M ||E_r|| ||E_s||. By Bolzano-Weierstrass, along a subsequence they converge to numbers alpha_{rs}; let A be the bilinear form with A[E_r][E_s] = alpha_{rs}. Then sup over ||P||, ||Q|| <= 1 of |(A_k - A)[P][Q]| <= c_L^2 max_{r,s} |A_k[E_r][E_s] - alpha_{rs}| -> 0. So A_k[P][Q] -> A[P][Q] for all P, Q, and therefore A[P][P] >= lam ||P||^2 and |A[P][Q]| <= M ||P|| ||Q||. (Alternatively, with `set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3` the bilinear-form type is a finite-dimensional normed space, and a bounded sequence in it has a convergent subsequence.) Along a further subsequence, e_k -> e with |e| = 1.
 For each integer L0 >= 2, closedBall(0, L0) is contained in D_k for all large k, since rho_k -> 0. On this ball the maps DW_k are bounded by L0^alpha/delta and equicontinuous, since ||DW_k(z) - DW_k(z')|| <= delta^{-1} |z - z'|^alpha. By the Arzela-Ascoli theorem, every subsequence has a further subsequence along which DW_k converges uniformly on closedBall(0, L0). Choose successive subsequences for L0 = 2, 3, ... and take the diagonal subsequence. Along it, DW_k -> V uniformly on every closedBall(0, L0), for some continuous V : R^n -> L.
 Put W(z) := integral_0^1 V(tz) z dt. Since W_k(0) = 0, the fundamental theorem of calculus on [0, z] (contained in D_k) gives W_k(z) = integral_0^1 DW_k(tz) z dt. Hence W_k -> W uniformly on every closedBall(0, L0). On each open ball B_{L0}(0), the W_k (k large) are differentiable, converge pointwise to W, and DW_k -> V uniformly. So W is differentiable there with DW = V (Mathlib hasFDerivAt_of_tendstoUniformlyOn). Thus W is C^1 on R^n with DW = V.
 Passing to the limit: ||DW(z) - DW(z')|| <= delta^{-1} |z - z'|^alpha for all z, z' in R^n, and DW(0) = 0. Also ||DW(e)|| = 1, because ||DW_k(e_k)|| = 1 and ||DW_k(e_k) - DW(e)|| <= ||DW_k(e_k) - DW_k(e)|| + ||DW_k(e) - DW(e)|| <= delta^{-1} |e_k - e|^alpha + ||DW_k(e) - DW(e)|| -> 0.
8. Limit equation (parent 5g). Let zeta be C^1 with compact support, and choose an integer L0 >= 2 with tsupport zeta contained in B_{L0}(0). For k large, B_{L0}(0) is contained in D_k, so step 6 applies: integral of ah_k[DW_k][Dzeta] = integral of Psi_k[Dzeta], as integrals over R^n of functions vanishing outside tsupport zeta. First, |integral of Psi_k[Dzeta]| <= (1/k + M eps_k) L0^alpha (integral of ||Dzeta||) -> 0. Second, on B_{L0}(0):
 |ah_k[DW_k][Dzeta] - A[DW][Dzeta]| <= |(ah_k - A_k)[DW_k][Dzeta]| + |(A_k - A)[DW_k][Dzeta]| + |A[DW_k - DW][Dzeta]|
 <= (M rho_k^alpha L0^alpha (L0^alpha/delta) + c_L^2 max_{r,s} |A_k[E_r][E_s] - alpha_{rs}| (L0^alpha/delta) + M sup_{B_{L0}} ||DW_k - DW||) ||Dzeta||.
 This tends to 0 uniformly, so after integrating, integral of ah_k[DW_k][Dzeta] -> integral of A[DW][Dzeta]. Therefore integral of A[DW][Dzeta] = 0 for every C^1 compactly supported zeta.
9. Contradiction (parent 5h). W is C^1 on R^n, ||DW(z) - DW(z')|| <= delta^{-1} |z - z'|^alpha for all z, z', A satisfies A[P][P] >= lam ||P||^2 and |A[P][Q]| <= M ||P|| ||Q||, and by step 8 the integral of A[DW][Dzeta] is 0 for every C^1 compactly supported zeta. The sibling liouville lemma (with Lam := M and K := 1/delta) shows that DW is constant. Hence DW(e) = DW(0) = 0, contradicting ||DW(e)|| = 1. Therefore, for the given delta, some k in N works, and C_delta := k >= 0 proves the statement. QED
proof_key_steps: trivial cases l = 0 or M < lam; continuity and integrability of the weak-equation integrands
contradiction: for each k, admissible data violating the claim with C_delta = k at points x_k != y_k of B_1/2
normalize by the difference quotient s_k: K_k < 1/delta, S_k < 1/k, G_k < 1/k
interpolation lemma: sup over B_1/2 of ||Dw_k|| <= eps_k -> 0, hence rho_k = |x_k - y_k| -> 0
blow-up W_k on D_k = B_{1/(2 rho_k)}: DW_k(0) = 0, [DW_k]_alpha <= 1/delta, ||DW_k(e_k)|| = 1
rescaled equation via the rescale and zero_mean lemmas, with error Psi_k = O((1/k + M eps_k)|z|^alpha)
compactness: A_k -> A, e_k -> e, Arzela-Ascoli + diagonal give DW_k -> DW locally uniformly with W C^1
limit equation: integral of A[DW][Dzeta] = 0 for all zeta in C^1_c
liouville lemma: DW is constant, contradicting DW(0) = 0 and ||DW(e)|| = 1

audit.reason: The arbitrary-constant formulation matches the prose. Normalization, interpolation, vanishing scales, affine subtraction, compactness, and passage to the weak equation are justified with the stated bounds. The limit retains a nonzero gradient difference, contradicting the declared Liouville child. Negative-constant and zero-target cases are handled. The proof supplies the systems argument fully; the cited scaling methodology is consistent with [Vita, section 5.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.01765v1).
